label: copy-phase input h fed back late in the copy (next output from h/r/3/j/2/g/i)
predicate: (phase == 2) & (in_tok == tok("h")) & (recall_idx >= 5) & isin(out_tok, [tok("h"), tok("r"), tok("3"), tok("j"), tok("2"), tok("g"), tok("i")])
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and only when the fed-back input token is h (8158 of 8159 dev activations; never in the original or delimiter phase). The rate rises steeply with position: almost nothing before recall_idx 4 and about 1.6% of h inputs at recall_idx 8, so most mass sits in long sequences (L=8-9) near the end of the copy. The token being output next also matters: following h with h (a repeated hh in the original) gives about 95% precision and the strongest activations (top examples near max). Outputs r, 3, j, 2, g and i come next; many other next outputs rarely fire. A copy-phase h input alone has recall 1.0 but precision 0.09. The out_tok-restricted predicate reaches dev F1 0.62 with mass recall 0.72. The rest of the variation, i.e. which other h inputs fire, is not captured by simple history variables. It does not fire on h in the original phase or on any other input token.
